scope.basis: APP11 static family semantics are primary. APP10 and APP11 have a checked shared schema and identical normalized ADC getter/calculation instructions; historical CAL values belong to distinct specimens.
scope.interpretation: Descriptions concern software use of CAL families, not correct values for a specimen, physical response, or live calibration.
scope.row_boundary: A family-level description does not by itself establish the consumer of every individual CAL row.

AciGain.summary: Selected ACI range gain scales amplitude in the ordinary result path.
limitations: Noise-calibration, self-test, overload and rolldown branches can change the downstream path.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded ordinary ACI result path

AciSqNoise.summary: Selected ACI range squared-noise term adjusts the second moment before the ordinary result is assembled.
limitations: Noise-calibration and self-test use separate branches.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded ordinary ACI result path

AcvGain.summary: Selected ACV range gain scales the ordinary result and participates in overload and rolldown handling.
limitations: The debug overload-disable branch bypasses ordinary overload and rolldown operations.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded ordinary ACV result path

AcvMedIirDenomCoef.summary: MED low-frequency calibration stores a fitted IIR denominator; the software recurrence consumes its Q20 coefficients.
limitations: The two fit points do not establish a physical frequency axis, sampling cadence, or complete transfer response.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded MED fit and software recurrence

AcvMedIirNumeratorCoef.summary: MED low-frequency calibration stores a fitted numerator; the normalizer derives coefficient constants and their squares from it.
limitations: A physical transfer response and sampling cadence are outside this software evidence.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded MED coefficient path

AcvSlowDcGainSquared.summary: A named SLOW CAL state has a getter; a separate Compute DC-gain setter stores its argument plus one.
limitations: A path from this CAL state to that setter or a numeric consumer in the checked ordinary SLOW path has not been established.
This does not establish that the state is globally unused.

evidence.scope: APP11 separate state/getter and Compute setter; connection open

AcvSlowIirDenomCoef.summary: SLOW low-frequency calibration stores a fitted IIR denominator; the software recurrence consumes its Q20 coefficients.
limitations: The two fit points do not establish a physical frequency axis, sampling cadence, or complete transfer response.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded SLOW fit and software recurrence

AcvSlowIirNumeratorCoef.summary: SLOW low-frequency calibration stores a fitted numerator; the normalizer derives coefficient constants and their squares from it.
limitations: A physical transfer response and sampling cadence are outside this software evidence.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded SLOW coefficient path

AcvSlowNoiseGainSquared.summary: A SLOW or MED noise-gain state selected by mode; its runtime setter stores input plus one and its getter returns state minus one.
limitations: The setter/getter transformation alone does not describe the complete AC output path.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded setter/getter path

AcvSqNoise.summary: Selected ACV range squared-noise term adjusts the second moment before the ordinary result is assembled.
limitations: This is distinct from the mode-selected AcvSlowNoiseGainSquared state.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded ordinary ACV result path

AdcQuad.summary: The selected DCV quadratic coefficient contributes a square term when the quadratic mode byte is enabled.
limitations: Other modes use the affine path; overload guards can bypass the final consumer.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded DCV quadratic branch

Adc_DcOffset.summary: DcOffset D sets the common level of the 64-entry alternating ADC offset LUT: D+P and D−P.
limitations: The LUT affects feedback-code history; D is not directly added to the final reading.

evidence.scope: APP11 ADC getter and register calculation
Checked APP10/APP11 arithmetic and bounded ADC interpretation

Adc_FineMergeGain.summary: FineMergeGain is rounded after multiplication by 65536 and reduced to low 10 bits for the merge field that scales the fine-code difference.
limitations: Quantization and low-bit selection matter; the stored double is not a direct volts-per-count reading gain.

evidence.scope: APP11 ADC getter and register calculation
Checked APP10/APP11 arithmetic and bounded ADC interpretation

Adc_FineSamplOffset.summary: FineSamplOffset is transformed with the decision count into the fine-trigger register; in the ordinary positive domain F is (trunc(offset)+N−2) remainder N.
limitations: The stored offset is not itself the trigger register value; the expression has a bounded input domain.

evidence.scope: APP11 ADC getter and register calculation
Checked APP10/APP11 arithmetic and bounded ADC interpretation

Adc_Jitter.summary: Jitter supplies the low-three-bit parameter of a separate deterministic digital J generator.
limitations: The CAL scalar, control bits and generated signed J are distinct; J is already included in feedback code C, not an extra addition to the reading or a clock-jitter measure.

evidence.scope: APP11 ADC getter and register calculation
Bounded downstream meaning of ADC J

Adc_LutGain.summary: LutGain scales a 256-entry coarse-indexed LUT; each entry is rounded and clamped to the integer range −64 through 63.
limitations: The table changes feedback-code selection; it does not independently multiply a completed reading.

evidence.scope: APP11 ADC getter and register calculation
Checked APP10/APP11 arithmetic and bounded ADC interpretation

Adc_N_Decisions.summary: N_Decisions sets the ADC decision count N and a software cycle field of N−1.
limitations: It also enters trigger positions and should be read with the other timing fields.

evidence.scope: APP11 ADC getter and register calculation
Checked APP10/APP11 ADC timing interpretation

Adc_Nf_Slope.summary: Nf_Slope forms decision-window half-width H by truncating slope/2; H enters the calculated coarse, start and end positions.
limitations: Its meaning depends on the decision count and fine-aperture position; it is not a result multiplier.

evidence.scope: APP11 ADC getter and register calculation
Checked APP10/APP11 ADC timing interpretation

Adc_PiOffset.summary: PiOffset P sets the alternating component of the ADC offset LUT: D+P and D−P.
limitations: It is not a direct reading offset or an established cancellation of the analog geometry term.

evidence.scope: APP11 ADC getter and register calculation
Bounded downstream ADC offset interpretation

CapOffset.summary: Terminal-selected capacitance offset, stored in farads, is subtracted in the software capacitance result path.
limitations: Software units do not establish calibration accuracy or identify a particular external capacitance.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded CAP getter and result calculation
APP11 CAP range scale, unit labels and unchanged result transfer

CurrentSrcDelay.summary: For the checked compensated low-range resistance path, software selects the unsigned maximum of this state and PacketCounts.McDelay as a count of short DC MeanPacket records before NPLC accumulation. APP11 minimum-sample-time arithmetic uses an initialized scale of 19.952941176 microseconds per count.
limitations: The time estimate describes this CAL count only; a later trigger-delay maximum can extend the wait. One wait is not the complete autozero cycle. This software scale is not a measured hardware clock.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded software timing-state path
APP11 RES minimum-sample-time arithmetic and initialized seconds/count scale

DciGain.summary: One of six DCI range gains is selected and scaled by total packet weight in the common setter.
limitations: Line-frequency and row-index selection follow the checked software path; an index accepted by its guard is not necessarily a valid NPLC enum.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded DCI range and setter path

DciOff.summary: DCI range and terminal selection choose a front or rear offset, which the common setter scales by total packet weight with sign-dependent rounding.
limitations: The interpretation applies to the checked range and terminal branches.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded DCI offset path

DcvGain.summary: One of five DCV range gains is selected and scaled by total packet weight in the common setter.
limitations: A row index accepted by the software guard is not necessarily a valid NPLC enum.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded DCV range and setter path

DcvOff.summary: DCV range and terminal selection choose a front or rear offset, which the common setter scales by total packet weight with sign-dependent rounding.
limitations: The CAP dependency applies only to two specified 10 V offset members; it is not a property of every row.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded DCV offset path

Divider10M.summary: A conditional correction for ordinary high-range resistance results, applied below its checked guard.
limitations: Above the guard the path selects overload; a global override changes the additional upper limit.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded ordinary RES range 6/7 path

FreqGain.summary: Frequency counter scale used in software frequency and period calculations, and in the CAP denominator path.
limitations: Counter rollover and physical timing behavior are outside the checked chain.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded frequency, period and CAP calculations

HeaterGain.summary: Heater drive calculation divides its positive-target square-root term by HeaterGain before code scaling.
limitations: Nonpositive target power and voltage-compensation guards use separate branches; hardware output is unverified.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded heater-code calculation

HeaterRes.summary: Heater drive calculation multiplies HeaterRes by positive target power inside the square-root term.
limitations: Nonpositive target power and voltage-compensation guards use separate branches; hardware output is unverified.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded heater-code calculation

McDelay.summary: A CAL-state change raises an APP11 update event that can reach register writes.
limitations: Those writes are not proof of numeric use: PacketCounts.McDelay comes from mcDelayTable, with no established link from this CAL value.

evidence.scope: APP11 event-to-write path; numeric CAL-to-table link open

MzDelay.summary: A CAL-state change raises an APP11 update event that can reach register writes.
limitations: Those writes are not proof of numeric use: PacketCounts.MzDelay comes from mzDelayTable, with no established link from this CAL value.

evidence.scope: APP11 event-to-write path; numeric CAL-to-table link open

PrechargePwm.summary: A software PWM control value converted through integer and low-16-bit steps before an upper clamp and control write.
limitations: Conversion order is material: this is not a simple clamp to 0–255, and no lower clamp is shown; physical PWM output is unverified.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded digital writer path

Res4Gain.summary: Four-wire resistance selects a gain bank by range and offset-compensation branch, then scales by total packet weight.
limitations: CAP dependence is limited to five named members; high ranges also have a conditional Divider10M correction.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded four-wire RES path

Res4Off.summary: Four-wire resistance selects an offset bank by range, terminals and offset-compensation branch, then scales by total packet weight with sign-dependent rounding.
limitations: Front/rear and offset-compensation states are separate banks.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded four-wire RES path

ResGain.summary: Two-wire resistance selects an ordinary or offset-compensated gain bank by range, then scales by total packet weight.
limitations: The ordinary high-range path may also apply a guarded Divider10M correction.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded two-wire RES path

ResOff.summary: Two-wire resistance selects an offset bank by range, terminals and offset-compensation branch, then scales by total packet weight with sign-dependent rounding.
limitations: Front/rear and offset-compensation states are separate banks.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded two-wire RES path

flatness.summary: Per-range ACI and ACV FIR coefficient vectors passed as signed low-16-bit words through the ordinary firmware writer.
limitations: These are vectors, not individually known frequency taps; firmware writes do not prove FPGA acceptance or an instrument frequency response.

evidence.scope: APP11 770-row source-to-holder and ordinary writer binding

lp.summary: Shared ACI and ACV low-pass FIR coefficient vectors passed as signed low-16-bit words through the ordinary firmware writer.
limitations: These are vectors, not individually known frequency taps; firmware writes do not prove FPGA acceptance or an instrument frequency response.

evidence.scope: APP11 140-row source-to-holder and ordinary writer binding
